FRONTEND: TheftConfirm.js named-import of IrisFullscreenWizard works (no render crash on error path). When the email-confirm GET resolves to OK, the page renders 'Récupération validée' + Étape 2 iris card + theft-iris-confirm-btn ('Lancer la vérification iris'). Click opens IrisFullscreenWizard TRULY FULLSCREEN (1280×900 bounding box on a 1280×900 viewport — the iter70 createPortal(document.body) fix carries through). iris-cancel closes the wizard cleanly. Step-0 testids verified by code-review (line 515-522 BiometricEnrollmentField.jsx: iris-approach-progress only when `step === 0 && streamReady`, iris-progress only when `step >= 2 && step <= 4`). Camera is denied in headless Chromium → status 'Impossible d'accéder à la caméra…' is shown and streamReady stays false → approach-progress correctly absent. ONE NEW UX BUG FOUND in TheftConfirm.js: React.StrictMode + dev build causes the useEffect to fire twice → first GET consumes the token (DB: used:True), second GET returns 404 → state ends at 'error' even with a freshly-seeded valid token. To complete the success-path Playwright test I had to network-mock the endpoint. In a prod build (no StrictMode double-mount) the flow works as designed, but this is still a robustness gap that costs idempotency on any remount.

ui_bugs.issue: React.StrictMode double-mount in dev causes /auth/theft-email-confirm to be called twice. The endpoint is single-use: 1st call marks used:True, 2nd call returns 404 → final state is 'error' even with a fresh valid token. Reproduction: seed theft_email_tokens with a token, visit /theft-confirm?token=…, observe DB shows used:True AND UI shows 'Échec / Lien invalide ou déjà utilisé.'. The `cancelled` flag in the cleanup function only suppresses setState — it does NOT abort the in-flight request. Fix: gate the axios call with a useRef sentinel (e.g. `if (firedRef.current) return; firedRef.current = true;`) or wrap with AbortController. In production builds StrictMode does not double-fire so end-users won't see this, but any future legitimate remount (e.g. Suspense, route change) would also burn the token.

action_items: (MEDIUM) TheftConfirm.js: guard the email-confirm useEffect against double-fire (useRef sentinel or AbortController). Otherwise StrictMode burns the token on first render and the success UI is unreachable in dev.

(LOW) Optional: make /auth/theft-email-confirm idempotent for ~5s after first success (return cached {success, revoked_count}) so a benign double-fire does not show 404 to the user. Adds resilience for back/forward nav too.

rca of the issue: ROOT CAUSE of the TheftConfirm dev-only 'Échec on valid token': React.StrictMode in /app/frontend/src/index.js line 12 wraps <App/>, which in dev intentionally double-invokes useEffect to surface side-effect bugs. The TheftConfirm useEffect calls axios.get('/auth/theft-email-confirm') without a useRef guard, so both renders fire the GET. The first GET succeeds → server marks the token used:True. The second GET returns 404 → state ends at 'error'. The `cancelled` flag only blocks setState from the FIRST request after unmount; it does not abort either network call. MITIGATION (canonical): add `const firedRef = useRef(false); useEffect(() => { if (firedRef.current) return; firedRef.current = true; … }, [token]);` — 3 lines. Or make the endpoint idempotent server-side. The bug does NOT manifest in production builds because StrictMode's double-fire is dev-only, but the underlying race (any legitimate remount burns the token) is real and warrants the fix.
